ticket.title: GaugeblockPaths offers a ledger path but no records path, so consumers copy the wrong filename
ticket.description:
GaugeblockPaths exposes ledger() - the path to .gaugeblock/storypole/ledger.jsonl - and nothing for the layout tickets now use. Consumers therefore either spell tickets/KEY.json themselves or reach for the state through a store API, and the sweep that followed ADR 0009 found one consumer (benchwork context injection) that took the first route and silently lost all data when the layout changed. Add a records-aware accessor beside ledger() (the tickets directory, and a helper that reports which layout a store is in) and mark ledger() as the legacy layout in its doc comment, so the next reader has to choose deliberately rather than copying the ledger path because it is the only one offered. Cross-repo: this is the shared helper every tool uses to find storypole state.

SCOPE SHARPENED 2026-11-08, after a consumer sweep.

The failure that prompted this was not a library boundary breaking: every storypole_core API call site in
benchwork survived ADR 0009 untouched. The one site that broke spelled ledger.jsonl itself. So the deliverable
here is not just an accessor, it is making the wrong thing impossible:

  storypole_core::state::load(dot_dir) -> Result<LoadedState>

one call that returns the tasks and events of a store whichever layout it uses, replacing every consumer that
currently decides which file to read. benchwork's context injector becomes one line (GB-349); the same helper
serves chalkline, joiner and outfeed, which all depend on storypole-core already and would otherwise each
re-derive the rule.

Also offer the path accessor beside ledger() and mark ledger() as the legacy layout in its own doc comment,
so copying it requires choosing it rather than finding it alone.

Why not a CLI/MCP boundary or a consumer sub-crate instead: benchwork is a daemon serving a UI panel, so a
process spawn per task-list refresh and typed errors degrading to stderr are both real regressions; four
repositories already consume storypole-core in-process, so a one-consumer crate is not the shape of the problem;
and MCP is a protocol for agents, not IPC between two of our own daemons.

DONE 2026-11-08, in two commits, one per repository.

storypole (e92f032): storypole_core::state::load returns a store's tasks and events whichever layout holds them,
plus the layout it found. One call replaces "each consumer decides which file to read" for benchwork, chalkline,
joiner and outfeed. An absent store is empty rather than an error, because a panel should render nothing rather
than fail. Three tests: empty, records, legacy ledger.

common (33a3235): GaugeblockPaths gained storypole_tickets() beside ledger(), and ledger() now says in its own
comment that it is the legacy layout and that hard-coding it reads nothing in a migrated store. Both comments
point at state::load as the route to prefer, so the pair documents the right answer rather than only offering
paths.

Neither commit is invoked by a consumer yet - GB-349 is the first caller.
